summary: Slingshot's new-school big air kite built on an Aluula airframe with hybrid open-C canopy and a 6-point Trimflight bridle. Lightweight, rigid, and explosive — built for the new era of boosting where going higher is met with controlled confidence.
best_for: New school big air and megaloops

reviews.summary: Jason calls the NXT V2 his favorite 9m kite and the front-runner for kite of the year. Its low end is among the best he has tested, the bar is light and well balanced, and its boost and hangtime match the Evo and Rebel D/LAB on well-timed jumps. Its smooth, slightly full loop made it the most confidence-building Aluula kite he tested.

structured_review.summary: Jason Montreal's pick for the new big air/freeride benchmark. The V2 pairs top-tier boost and hangtime with excellent low end, light balanced bar pressure and an easy, confidence-building feel; he rode one 9m from about 20 to 40+ knots. The Evo D/LAB is slightly more explosive and the Rebel D/LAB steadier at the very top end.
pros: Low end among the best tested; Jason rode a 9m when lighter friends were on 10–11m
Light-to-moderate, well-balanced bar pressure with excellent bar-to-kite response
Monster boosting with a bigger sweet spot and better gust catch than V1
Most confidence-inspiring Aluula kite for technical kiteloop tricks
Huge wind range covers a one- or two-kite quiver
cons: Slightly less explosive off the water than the Evo D/LAB in light-to-moderate wind
Rebel D/LAB is more stable and consistent at the very top end (30–40 knots)
Loop is a touch fuller than the quickest Dacron or Brainchild loopers and can pause in gusts
Feels best on the Slingshot bar with 24m lines
structured_review.best_for: Intermediate to pro riders who want one Aluula kite for boosting, technical kiteloops and freeride across a huge wind range.
structured_review.not_for: Budget-conscious riders starting their very first kiteloops.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Jason Montreal's kite-of-the-year pick: monster boost, light bar, and a huge wind range.
